Nina (People Ops): @here New short policy updates going live June 1 — short TL;DR then links. Two items: paid time for vaccine appointments (global) + comp-time exceptions for major incident rotations. Please skim.
hr-bot: Policy pages updated: https://redwood.internal/hr/policies/vax-time-2026 and https://redwood.internal/hr/policies/comp-time-exceptions-2026 (version 2026-06-01)
Nina (People Ops): 1) Paid vaccine & booster time (global)
- What: Up to 8 hours/year paid time for COVID/vaccine-related appointments (employee + dependent vaccine appointments). This includes travel & recovery time where recommended by a clinician.
- How to request: Use HR portal -> Time Off -> Vaccination. For short appointments use the slack shortcut `/hr timeoff --type vaccine --hours 2 --date 2026-06-14` and choose whether it's for you or a dependent.
- Notes: If you need more than 8 hours for recovery (e.g., significant reaction) you can request comp-time or PTO; manager approval required. Local law supersedes if more generous.
Ken M.: Quick Q  does this cover employer-mandated on-site vaccine clinics (like if we run a clinic at HQ)?
Nina (People Ops): Yes, time spent at a company-run clinic counts against this 8-hour allowance but we recommend self-scheduling during workday where possible. If youre required to attend outside normal hours let us know and we can log as comp-time.
Zoe Lin: If Im remote in EMEA and need to travel to a clinic 90 minutes away, is travel time covered?
legal-bot: Travel time reasonable to access medical care is covered per policy; jurisdictional rules may vary. For long travel we ask you to attach a note in the portal and HR will confirm.
Nina (People Ops): 2) Comp-time exceptions for major incident rotations (pilot)
- What: During company-declared major incidents where teams run extended overnight rotations, managers may grant an extra 16 hours comp-time beyond the 40h cap for the single incident period.
- Rules: Extra comp-time must be scheduled and used within 30 days of the incident end. Manager approval required and People Ops will record the exception. This is a limited-scope escalation tool, not a substitute for staffing.
- Request flow: Manager files an incident-comp-time exception form in the HR portal; once approved, affected engineers receive a Slack DM with their updated balance.
hr-bot: Example command for on-call comp-time claim: `/hr comp-time request --hours 6 --date 2026-06-05 --incident ID:INC-2026-1337 --manager @rebecca` (manager approval recorded automatically)
Ken M.: If we use the extra 16h during an incident, does that reduce the usual 40h cap permanently?
Nina (People Ops): No, it's a one-time temporary increase for that incident window only. Your normal 40h cap returns after the exception period ends.
Zoe Lin: Will exceptions be audited? Curious about fairness across teams.
payroll-bot: All exception approvals and balances are logged. People Ops will review exception usage quarterly and produce a summary report (anonymized) for fairness checks.
Nina (People Ops): Final notes: vaccine time is available now for scheduling; comp-time exceptions require a declared incident and manager initiation. Office hours Wednesday 9am PT in #people-ops-office-hours for questions. If you have a personal case DM me. :syringe::sparkles:
